cases.provenance: Real NASA 2023 fact with a deliberately injected unit error in a synthetic derivative; not a real false NASA statement.
cases.a: NASA's 2023 annual global surface-temperature anomaly was about 1.2 degrees Celsius above the 1951–1980 average. The corresponding Fahrenheit anomaly was about 2.1 degrees Fahrenheit.
cases.b: Our summary of that same NASA 2023 annual global surface-temperature analysis gives an anomaly of 2.1 degrees Celsius above the 1951–1980 average. This number is in Celsius, not Fahrenheit.
cases.label: conflict
cases.reason: Same analysis, year and baseline; 1.2 C and 2.1 C disagree. B has an injected unit-transcription error.

cases.a: For release Orion 4.2, the completed audit states that unsigned extensions are not permitted to execute under the default configuration. No exception is described.
cases.b: For release Orion 4.2 under its default configuration, unsigned extensions are permitted to execute. This is a summary of the completed audit, and no exception applies.
cases.label: conflict
cases.reason: Opposite permission statements about the same release and default configuration.

cases.a: The final settled refund for invoice INV-204 on 2025-02-18 was exactly USD 138.00, including all adjustments. This is the total refund, not one installment.
cases.b: The final settled refund for invoice INV-204 on 2025-02-18 was exactly USD 183.00, including all adjustments. This is the total refund, not one installment.
cases.label: conflict
cases.reason: Different exact final totals for the same invoice, date and currency.

cases.a: The final audit of batch B17 found that all 37 units passed the insulation test. There were zero failures and no excluded units.
cases.b: The final audit of batch B17 found that unit B17-09 failed the insulation test. It is one of the same 37 included units. These are the final results before any repair or retest.
cases.label: conflict
cases.reason: All included units passed versus an included unit failed in the same final test.

cases.a: Rule R5, effective 2025-06-01, grants eligibility to applicants aged 18 or older on the filing date. An applicant exactly 18 is eligible if the other requirements are met.
cases.b: For the same R5 rule effective 2025-06-01, an applicant exactly 18 on the filing date is ineligible despite satisfying all other requirements. Eligibility begins strictly above age 18.
cases.label: conflict
cases.reason: Inclusion and exclusion of the same boundary-age applicant under the same rule.

cases.a: The signed FINAL revision 3 of report Q7 records exactly 420 completed jobs for region North during April 2025. It supersedes revision 2, which recorded 390 jobs.
cases.b: According to the signed FINAL revision 3 of report Q7, region North completed exactly 390 jobs during April 2025. This figure refers to revision 3, not the superseded revision 2.
cases.label: conflict
cases.reason: Same explicit final revision, region and month; conflicting counts. The old revision number does not resolve B's claim.

cases.provenance: Short author-written paraphrases of real NASA and NOAA publications; no injected error.
cases.a: NASA reports a 2023 global surface-temperature anomaly of about 1.2 C above its 1951–1980 reference average.
cases.b: NOAA reports a 2023 global land-and-ocean temperature anomaly of 1.18 C above the 20th-century reference average. NOAA uses its own analysis and this different reference period.
cases.label: compatible
cases.reason: Different analysis and reference baseline; the numerical difference alone is not a contradiction.

cases.a: In March 2025, North branch processed exactly 138 completed refunds. This count covers March only.
cases.b: In April 2025, North branch processed exactly 183 completed refunds. This count covers April only.
cases.label: compatible
cases.reason: Different months, so both counts can hold.

cases.provenance: Wholly synthetic controlled example using a standard unit conversion.
cases.a: At the single recorded checkpoint, sensor T3 measured the sample temperature as 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
cases.b: For the same sensor T3 checkpoint and sample, the reported temperature was 0 degrees Celsius. This report converts the original Fahrenheit reading.
cases.label: compatible

cases.a: The measured defect rate increased from exactly 8% to exactly 10%. That is an increase of 2 percentage points.
cases.b: For the same measured defect rate, the change from exactly 8% to exactly 10% was a 25% relative increase, computed relative to the initial 8% rate.
cases.label: compatible
cases.reason: Two percentage points and 25 percent relative increase describe the same change.

cases.a: During March 2025, North branch had an exactly 10% refund rate across all eligible orders.
cases.b: North branch had an exactly 12% refund rate across all eligible orders. The observation period is not specified, and no date is supplied elsewhere in this record.
cases.label: insufficient
cases.reason: B lacks a period; cannot establish either same-period contradiction or different-period compatibility.

cases.a: Survey S9 reports 1,000 completed responses from first-time customers during June 2025.
cases.b: The June 2025 customer survey reports 2,000 completed responses. It does not identify the survey version or whether respondents are first-time customers, returning customers, or both.
cases.label: insufficient
cases.reason: Missing population and survey identity prevent a definitive contradiction judgment.
